 SALEM, Ore. - The Oregon Department of Human Services is encouraging people to apply for food assistance now to see if they qualify before the holidays.
 SNAP provides monthly food benefits to help households buy groceries. The agency wants every person who qualifies for SNAP to receive it, and applying now gives the department time to process applications before the holidays.
 For people already receiving SNAP, seasonal employment may offer another opportunity. Seasonal jobs at pumpkin patches, Halloween stores, Christmas tree farms or picking up extra hours during the holidays could help people meet federal SNAP work or activity rules or regain benefits they've previously lost.
 "Seasonal employment can be an opportunity to earn extra income while also helping people meet SNAP work or activity rules," said Jessica Amaya Hoffman, ODHS interim Oregon Eligibility Partnership Director. "If you've started a new job, picked up additional hours or are planning to work during the holidays, contact us. We can help you understand how your work and income affect your SNAP benefits and what steps you may need to take."
 Under federal rules, certain adults ages 18 through 64 must complete at least 80 hours of work or qualifying activities each month to continue receiving SNAP benefits, unless they qualify for an exemption. Seasonal employment, including jobs at Halloween stores, retail businesses, restaurants, warehouses and other employers preparing for the holidays, may help people meet these requirements.
 If you're picking up a second job or working extra hours during the holidays, it's important to understand how this income may affect your SNAP benefits. Households must report income changes when required under SNAP reporting rules so benefits can be calculated accurately.
 People who have already lost SNAP benefits because they did not meet work or activity rules may also be able to regain eligibility through employment or other qualifying activities. People may need to reapply for benefits and demonstrate that they meet the requirements.
 The agency encourages people to contact the ODHS ABAWD Team to discuss their circumstances, report qualifying hours and learn what steps they need to take to keep or regain benefits. Some people may qualify for an exemption from SNAP work or activity rules, which would automatically exempt them from upcoming Oregon Health Plan work or activity rules scheduled to begin in January 2027.
 The department reminds everyone who receives benefits to keep their contact information, including mailing address, up to date. Important notices may include information about eligibility, work or activity rules, deadlines or actions needed to keep benefits.
 People can visit the agency's website or contact their local ODHS office for assistance.
